You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-005","because":"Two cooling systems in one data center failed simultaneously while outside temperatures were extraordinarily high, matching the rule's conditions for treating redundant cooling failure as a single-point-of-failure event.","signals":["GCP-LDN-2022:S34","GCP-LDN-2022:S30"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"With mechanical cooling affected and no confirmation yet that it is running, the site must be treated as running on a load-dependent thermal buffer and action taken before automated shutdowns begin.","signals":["GCP-LDN-2022:S34","GCP-LDN-2022:S35"]},{"rule_id":"R-006","because":"Cooling capacity is in question and temperatures are at risk of exceeding safe operating thresholds, so progressive thermal load reduction should be considered before full shutdown.","signals":["GCP-LDN-2022:S34","GCP-LDN-2022:S30"]},{"rule_id":"R-014","because":"Multiple cooling systems are affected and manual intervention may be required, so extra technicians should be staged before attempting manual restarts.","signals":["GCP-LDN-2022:S34","GCP-LDN-2022:S35"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify whether mechanical cooling systems are still running and assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature; if not, plan to power down servers to prevent a longer outage or damage.","rule_id":"R-005"},{"action":"Treat the thermal buffer as finite and act before it is depleted; expect automated device shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Progressively decrease thermal load, considering termination of non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs, before resorting to full server shutdown.","rule_id":"R-006"},{"action":"Increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly and in parallel across data halls.","rule_id":"R-014"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"incident commander","reason":"Simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures means the data center may be unable to maintain a safe operating temperature, and thermal buffer depletion or automated shutdowns may be imminent."},"not_covered":["No rule addresses the specific cause of the cooling-system issue (e.g., water/air ingress, chiller cluster binding, or control-system failover) because the first-hour signals do not yet identify the failure mechanism.","No rule covers the initial alerting and investigation workflow itself; the pill assumes cooling loss is already confirmed or strongly suspected.","No rule addresses coordination with the utility provider or storm-related power quality beyond the voltage-swell scenario in R-001, which is not yet evidenced in the signals."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"One of the data centers that hosts zone europe-west2-a could not maintain a safe operating temperature due to a simultaneous failure of multiple, redundant cooling systems combined with the extraordinarily high outside temperatures."},{"id":"F2","kind":"response","text":"As data center temperatures started to increase, on Tuesday, 19 July 2022 at 08:06 US/Pacific Compute Engine terminated 42% of the Preemptible VMs (PVMs) across the europe-west2 region to reduce thermal load in zone europe-west2-a and ensure space for zonal failover activities in zones europe-west2-b and europe-west2-c."},{"id":"F3","kind":"response","text":"At 10:05, our engineers decided to power down servers in the impacted data center within europe-west2-a to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure in the zone."},{"id":"F4","kind":"remediation","text":"We will investigate and develop more advanced methods to progressively decrease the thermal load within a single data center space, reducing the probability that a full shutdown is required."},{"id":"F5","kind":"remediation","text":"Google engineers will be conducting an audit of cooling system equipment and standards across the data centers that house Google Cloud globally."},{"id":"F6","kind":"impact","text":"The total duration of the cooling system failure impact was 4 hours, 8 minutes."}]}
